etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle French jacquet, diminutive of Old French jaque.

definitions.definition: A piece of clothing worn on the upper body outside a shirt or blouse, often waist length to thigh length.
A piece of a person's suit, beside trousers and, sometimes, waistcoat; coat (US)
A protective or insulating cover for an object (e.g. a book, hot water tank, bullet.)

quote.citation: 1995 September 13, Richard Price, Spike Lee, 00:27:05 from the start, in Clockers, spoken by Rodney Little (Delroy Lindo), 40 Acres and a Mule Filmworks; distributed by Universal Pictures:
quote.text: We got a crowd of black, white customers, out-of-state license plates, what have you. Somebody gonna check that out. They gonna drop a dime on me, call 911. And you know with my jacket I can't go back to jail.

quote.citation: 1995 September 13, Richard Price, Spike Lee, 00:43:50 from the start, in Clockers, spoken by Rocco Klein (Harvey Keitel), 40 Acres and a Mule Filmworks; distributed by Universal Pictures:
quote.text: Yo's jacket shows possession with intent, possession of unlicensed firearm, and assault, for which he still owes three years.
"I need to look up somebody's jacket."

definitions.definition: (military) In ordnance, a strengthening band surrounding and reinforcing the tube in which the charge is fired.
The tough outer skin of a baked potato.
(Jamaica) A bastard child, in particular one whose father is unaware that he is not the child’s biological father.
To confine (someone) to a straitjacket. [from 18th c.]

quote.citation: 1792, Thomas Holcroft, Anna St. Ives, volume VII, Fragment:
quote.text: ‘None of your gab, I tell you! If you speak another word, I'll have you jacketed  […] !’

definitions.definition: (transitive) To enclose or encase in a jacket or other covering. [from 19th c.]

quote.citation: 1897, Alexander James Wallis-Tayler, Motor Cars Or Power-carriages for Common Roads‎[1]:
quote.text: ...to...prevent...the loss of heat...there is also a layer of silicate cotton or slag wool. This latter material is also employed to jacket the chimney for a certain portion of its length.
